rationale: Genome-wide Brunello knockout FACS screen on the YFP-CL1 degradation reporter in MelJuSo cells, two independent experiments (R1, R2), each with an unsorted pool and the ~0.5% YFP-low and YFP-high tails; column names match the GSM titles. The paper ran MAGeCK per experiment, sorted bin versus the unsorted pool (Supplementary Data 1), and took genes enriched in both experiments. Primary analysis: YFP-low vs unsorted (suppressors of degradation such as EIF5A are enriched in low), 2 vs 2. Second analysis: YFP-high vs unsorted, the paper's positive-control arm (UBE2G2, RNF139). No experiment term: with it only 1 residual df would remain, and the sorted libraries do not correlate more within an experiment than across. Library totals. The sorted libraries are heavily bottlenecked (10-36% zero guides, Spearman 0.2-0.4 with any other library), so single-guide jackpots are expected.
